item.title: Most Consumer Platforms Rife With Dark Patterns Despite Regulatory Action: Survey
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Nearly three-quarters of consumer companies that declared themselves free of dark patterns to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) continue…
item.content:encoded:
Nearly three-quarters of consumer companies that declared themselves free of dark patterns to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) continue to deploy deceptive user-interface practices, despite fresh regulations against such practices set to take effect on January 1.

A study commissioned by LocalCircles analysed 354 widely used online platforms across 45 sectors, drawing on consumer complaints, social media reports and the company’s AI-powered dark pattern detection engine.

The number of companies submitting self-declarations to the CCPA rose to 31 in November from 23 in July. However, platforms operated by 23 of these companies (74%) still contained dark patterns, the study found.

Across the broader sample, 94% of platforms, or 334 out of 354, exhibited at least one dark pattern. Only 20 platforms were found to be free of such practices.

Listed companies fared no better. Of the 108 consumer-facing platforms operated by companies listed on Indian stock exchanges, 102 (94%) continued to feature dark patterns.

In 37 of the 45 sectors examined, not a single platform was found to be compliant. These included online grocery, food delivery, online banking, taxi aggregators, OTT streaming and edtech.

B2B business marketplaces were the only category to achieve 100% compliance, followed by car rental platforms, where compliance stood at 25%. Sectors directly covered by anti-dark pattern protections also recorded low compliance rates. Ecommerce platforms had a compliance rate of just 17%, while quick commerce stood at 14%.

Forced action was the most prevalent dark pattern, appearing on 237 platforms (67%). Drip pricing was the second most common, at 63%, followed by bait and switch (50%) and interface interference (48%).

New Dark Pattern Rules Soon To Come Into Effect

The findings come ahead of the implementation of the Consumer Protection (Ecommerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, notified by the Department of Consumer Affairs in September.

The amended rules require ecommerce entities to:

  • Comply with dark pattern guidelines and conduct annual self-audits.
  • Prominently display a ‘dark-pattern-free’ compliance certificate.
  • Disclose the lowest price offered in the preceding 30 days when advertising discounts.
  • Avoid misleading search manipulation and clearly identify sponsored listings
  • Refrain from bundling fees for unrelated services.
  • Obtain express, affirmative consent for specified uses of consumer data.
  • Disclose product details, including ‘best before’ or ‘use before’ dates, along with relevant seller information.
  • Clearly provide return and refund policies, warranty information, delivery terms and payment details.

The findings also build on concerns raised during previous festive sales. We had reported last year on how dark patterns proliferated across ecommerce platforms during festive sales, nudging shoppers towards higher spending and purchases without adequate information.

Since the introduction of regulations prohibiting dark patterns, the CCPA has penalised several platforms, including IndiGo, Zepto, FirstCry, PhysicsWallah, BookMyShow, SpiceJet and Rapido, for deploying such practices.

Sectoral regulators, including the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), have also moved to strengthen consumer protections against dark patterns.

item.title: Shadowfax To Acquire WeFast To Expand Into Intra-City Deliveries
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Shadowfax has acquired the Indian entity of global same-day intra-city delivery platform Borzo (formerly known as WeFast) for ₹23.3 Cr,…
item.content:encoded:
Shadowfax has acquired the Indian entity of global same-day intra-city delivery platform Borzo (formerly known as WeFast) for ₹23.3 Cr, the logistics major disclosed today. 

With the acquisition, Shadowfax is set to enter on-demand intra-city goods transportation category and expand its reach into small and medium business (SME) and C2C deliveries. 

Shadowfax had earlier launched Shadowfax 360 to open its express parcel network to SMEs and D2C brands, and scaled the service up to over 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters. The deal now enables the company to extend the same model from parcel shipping to intra-city goods transportation. 

Founded in 2012 by Mike Alexandrovski, Aleks Shamis, and Dmitry Zubkov, Borzo had raised over $55 Mn from investors like Mubadala, AddVenture, Russian Direct Investment Fund, and Flashpoint. Founded in Russia and based in Amsterdam, it later relocated its headquarters to Mumbai in 2024. 

It currently operates in over five Indian cities with a fleet of over 32K delivery partners. The company claims it fulfils over 1.2 Cr deliveries annually. In CY25, it earned around ₹200 Cr in adjusted revenue. 

“Moving goods within cities is one of India’s largest logistics opportunities, and it has barely begun to go digital. Every day, shop owners, distributors and families still rely on phone calls and informal networks to get goods across town. That is set to change at scale, and Shadowfax intends to lead it,” added Shadowfax’s MD and CEO Abhishek Bansal. 

Founded in 2015 by Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, Shadowfax provides last-mile delivery services to ecommerce platforms and D2C brands. The company listed on the bourses in January after a ₹1,907 Cr IPO. 

On the financial front, Shadowfax’s consolidated net profit jumped over 5X YoY to ₹68 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue rose 56.6% to ₹1,537.7 Cr.

item.title: Maharashtra GST Authorities Search Turtlemint’s Insurance Broking Arm
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: Maharashtra GST authorities have initiated inspection, search and seizure proceedings against Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services (TIB), a wholly owned subsidiary…
item.content:encoded:
Maharashtra GST authorities have initiated inspection, search and seizure proceedings against Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services (TIB), a wholly owned subsidiary of listed insurtech company Turtlemint Fintech Solutions.

Turtlemint, in an exchange filing, said the proceedings began yesterday at the subsidiary’s registered office in Andheri East, Mumbai under Section 67 of the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The company did not disclose the specific alleged violations or a tax demand. It said the financial, operational, or other impact could not currently be quantified because the proceedings were ongoing.

“TIB is extending full cooperation to the concerned authorities and is providing the requisite information, documents and clarifications as may be required in connection with the proceedings,” it said.

Turtlemint added that regular business operations at both the parent company and its subsidiary remain unaffected. It said it would inform the stock exchanges of further developments, including the conclusion of the proceedings.

Inside Turtlemint’s Distribution Business

Founded in 2015 by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates an insurance distribution platform that enables financial advisors to sell motor, health, and life insurance.

Its model combines an advisor network with digital tools for comparing and selling policies, training, and back-end support. The company earns revenue through commissions and fees from insurers and other financial services providers.

Turtlemint had a digital partner network of over 6.59 Lakh at the end of FY26, following the addition of more than 1.15 Lakh partners during the year. It worked with 46 insurer partners and issued 7.83 Mn policies in FY26.

The GST proceedings come less than five months after the company’s stock market debut in June. Its ₹882.7 Cr IPO comprised a fresh issue of ₹660.7 Cr and an offer for sale of 1.46 Cr shares.

Its shares listed at ₹136.20 on the BSE, a 10.4% discount to the ₹152 issue price.

The GST action adds to regulatory concerns surrounding Turtlemint, whose shares have faced selling pressure following IRDAI’s draft proposals to cap insurance commissions, potentially squeezing its distribution revenue.

On the financial front, the company reported a 67% YoY reduction in its net loss to ₹25.8 Cr in Q2 FY27. Operating revenue increased 35.3% YoY to ₹342.2 Cr. Sequentially, revenue grew 16%, while net loss narrowed 32% from ₹37.8 Cr.

Shares of the company ended today’s trading session 0.60% lower at ₹64.63 on the BSE.

item.title: GMP Not Indicator Of Expected Returns: SEBI Seeks To Curb IPO GMP Circulation
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Markets regulator SEBI has moved to curb the publication and circulation of grey market premium (GMP) figures for upcoming IPOs.…
item.content:encoded:
Markets regulator SEBI has moved to curb the publication and circulation of grey market premium (GMP) figures for upcoming IPOs. The regulator has cautioned investors against treating such figures as indicators of potential listing gains.

In an advisory, the market regulator asked all SEBI-registered intermediaries and market participants to refrain from publishing GMP figures across communication channels.

For context, GMP refers to the unofficial premium at which shares are reportedly traded in the grey market before their formal listing on stock exchanges. Investors often track these figures to gauge market sentiment around an IPO and estimate potential listing gains before investing.

A rising GMP is generally interpreted as a sign of stronger demand and expectations of listing gains, while a falling or negative premium can signal weaker sentiment. 

Like the name suggests, such figures are speculative. However, reported premium offers an informal estimate of the price at which a company’s shares could list on stock exchanges. Investors use it to calculate potential gains if they receive an allotment and sell their shares after listing.

SEBI added that grey-market transactions take place outside its recognised framework, without any investor protection or a formal price-discovery mechanism. Consequently, investors relying heavily on GMP risk basing their subscription decisions on unofficial market sentiment rather than the company itself.

“The publication of such pre-listing premium figures may be detrimental to the interests of investors and contrary to the core principles of transparency and accountability in the securities market,” the regulator said.

SEBI FlagSEBIs Risks Around Unregulated GMP Transactions

SEBI’s advisory highlights the lack of regulatory oversight and investor protection in grey-market transactions.

Unlike trades conducted through recognised stock exchanges, grey-market transactions take place outside the formal securities market framework. They carry no settlement guarantee or investor protection and are not subject to a regulated price-discovery process

The regulator has clarified that investors involved in disputes arising from GMP transactions will not be able to access investor protection benefits under SEBI or stock exchange jurisdiction. They will also be unable to approach stock exchange grievance redressal mechanisms or the online dispute resolution (ODR) portal administered by exchanges and depositories.

SEBI has advised investors not to treat GMP as an indicator of an IPO’s likely listing price or expected returns. It has also urged them to avoid GMP-linked transactions and subscribe to IPOs exclusively through SEBI-registered intermediaries and authorised platforms.

The regulator further said that the publication, display, circulation or dissemination of unregulated pre-listing premiums across the securities market may be discontinued.

item.title: GalaxEye Awards Bellatrix Propulsion Contract For 30 Satellites
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye has awarded Bellatrix Aerospace a multi-year contract to supply propulsion systems for its next 30 Drishti…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye has awarded Bellatrix Aerospace a multi-year contract to supply propulsion systems for its next 30 Drishti Gen-II satellites, part of an OptoSAR constellation it aims to deploy by 2030.

Under the phased delivery schedule, Bellatrix will design, build, test, and deliver its Arka Hall-effect electric propulsion systems for the satellites. The companies did not disclose the contract value.

GalaxEye cofounder Pranit Mehta told Inc42 that deliveries will begin with systems for the first two satellites before scaling to the planned 30-satellite constellation. Bellatrix will be the programme’s primary propulsion supplier, he added.

Announced today at the fifth India International Space Conclave organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA), the agreement is India’s largest order between private space companies by satellite count, the startups claimed.

The propulsion systems will help move satellites from their initial drop-off orbits into assigned positions, maintain spacing across the constellation, avoid space debris, and deorbit at the end of their operational lives. 

Mehta said GalaxEye is also in active discussions with other Indian companies for its satellite programme, covering power systems, control systems, communications, and other subsystems.

“The Indian private ecosystem is here and now, and it is time that we partner with each other and not just rely on the government. The government has already done its job, and it is time for us to step up and help each other out,” he said.

Other Indian space companies also announced domestic partnerships at the conclave. Earth observation startup Pixxel signed MoUs with Centum Electronics and CS TECH Ai (Ceinsys Tech) to explore collaboration across satellite hardware, geospatial applications, and orbital sustainability.

With Centum, Pixxel will explore developing advanced electronics for satellite payloads and related subsystems. Its agreement with CS TECH Ai covers potential applications combining satellite data with geospatial analysis and engineering, including infrastructure monitoring.

The partnerships come as Pixxel looks to expand its satellite manufacturing and Earth intelligence capabilities  after raising $100 Mn in a Series C funding round earlier this year.

Building Beyond Mission Drishti

Founded in 2021 by Mehta, Suyash Singh, Denil Chawda, Kishan Thakkar, and Rakshit Bhatt, GalaxEye combines optical imaging and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) on a single satellite. Its OptoSAR technology supports Earth observation through clouds and at night for defence, agriculture, disaster management, maritime monitoring, and infrastructure.

The startup launched its first satellite under Mission Drishti aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in May. However, in July, it said it lost communication with the spacecraft following an anomaly it linked to a geomagnetic solar storm.

GalaxEye said the mission validated deployment, attitude control, onboard computing, and in-house mission operations. It subsequently outlined plans to launch two more OptoSAR satellites within 24 months while strengthening its engineering capabilities.

In September, GalaxEye secured a US patent for its OptoSAR technology, which synchronises optical and radar sensors. Later that month, the Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 Cr through optionally convertible debentures under the government’s Research, Development and Innovation Fund for multisensor satellite technology targeting imaging resolution finer than 0.5 metres.

The startup also acquired spacecraft engineering company StarOps in August to deepen its in-house capabilities.

Meanwhile, Bellatrix develops electric and green propulsion systems for satellites. Its Arka electric thrusters offer greater propellant efficiency than conventional chemical systems. The startup tested its propulsion technology aboard ISRO’s PSLV-C58 POEM-3 mission in January 2024.

Bellatrix raised $20 Mn (₹189.7 Cr) in a pre-Series B round led by Cactus Partners in March 2026 and is expanding manufacturing to serve satellite operators in India and overseas.

item.title: JioStar To Cut 150 Jobs To Control Costs
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Jio’s media arm, JioStar is reportedly looking to hand out the pink slip to about 150 employees. The job cuts…
item.content:encoded:
Jio’s media arm, JioStar is reportedly looking to hand out the pink slip to about 150 employees. The job cuts will impact multiple departments, including marketing, production, studios, and other operational functions. 

Industry sources suggest that the final number could be significantly higher. The impacted personnel will be offered a “substantial” severance package comprising a minimum of six months’ salary alongside a pro-rata bonus for the current financial year. 

Confirming the development, a JioStar spokesperson told Inc42, “We are rebalancing our portfolio to focus our investments on the businesses where we see the strongest opportunity for long-term growth. This is a strategic decision aimed at strengthening our competitive position in a dynamic and rapidly evolving industry. We recognise that these decisions will have an impact on some of our employees and we are committed to treating every colleague with respect and providing them every possible support through the transition.”

The development was first reported by exchange4media.

This is the second round of major job cuts at JioStar since the entity was formed by the merger of Reliance Industries-backed Viacom18 and Disney’s Star India. The merged entity was valued at $8.5 Bn (₹70,352 Cr) with Reliance holding a controlling stake, while Disney retained a significant minority interest. Reliance had also announced an investment of $1.4 Bn to support JioStar’s growth. 

Following the November 2024 amalgamation, JioStar executed an extensive restructuring in March 2025 that resulted in over 1,000 employees exiting. However, those layoffs were focused primarily on eliminating redundancies rather than to protect margins. 

The layoffs come amid a mixed financial performance for JioStar, with revenue growing but profitability coming under pressure.

For the September quarter (Q2 FY27), JioStar reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) increase in operating revenue to ₹6,806 Cr. However, EBITDA from operations fell 11% to ₹1,372 Cr, while operating EBITDA margin contracted 600 basis points to 22.1% from 28.1% a year earlier. Profit before tax also declined 14% to ₹1,139 Cr.

The company attributed the revenue growth to higher subscription income across digital and linear television, stronger digital entertainment advertising and increased sports advertising, supported by a higher number of cricketing events. 

Operationally, JioStar reported a 15% YoY increase in digital entertainment watch time during the quarter, driven by network general entertainment channels (GECs) and original content. It also said advertising revenue from digital entertainment grew on the back of higher connected TV (CTV) monetisation.

On the sports front, the India-West Indies series recorded 12% higher digital viewership and 13% higher CTV viewership than the England-India series in 2026. Meanwhile, the ongoing Premier League 2026-27 season saw digital viewership rise 25% and CTV viewership increase 13% compared with the previous season, based on data up to October 25, 2026.

JioStar also expanded JioHotstar into Singapore, the UK and Canada, reporting a 30% increase in its subscriber base following the international relaunch. The platform has additionally integrated food delivery services across its entertainment offering.

item.title: AidenAI Nets $32 Mn To Scale Enterprise AI Workflows
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment…
item.content:encoded:
Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities.

The fresh capital will be used to invest in its platform and engineering talent as it looks to scale its global enterprise AI business.

“With A91 as our partner, we are excited to invest in our people and platforms and help shape the next wave of enterprise technology services,” AidenAI founder and CEO Srinivas Kamadi said.

How AidenAI Builds Its Enterprise AI Business

Kamadi founded AidenAI in 2023 after spending nearly two decades with Infosys. 

Drawing on his experience of leading digital transformation at the company, Kamadi launched AidenAI to solve a recurring bottleneck faced by large enterprises: enterprise AI was stuck in the experimentation phase because outdated legacy systems made digital transformation too slow.

The New Jersey-based startup, whose majority of workforce is based out of Hyderabad, helps large enterprises integrate AI into existing applications, data infrastructure and business workflows. 

Its proprietary AI Builder Platform is designed to help businesses move beyond AI experimentation and deploy AI applications within their existing tech infrastructure. This platform connects with an enterprise’s existing systems and AI models, providing tools for AI agents. 

The startup also offers AiDAP, an AI-driven technology modernisation platform that helps enterprises modernise legacy software systems.

This positions AidenAI in the enterprise AI implementation market, where businesses are increasingly looking for solutions to integrate AI into business-critical operations rather than deploy standalone tools.

“While enterprise AI adoption is still in its early stages, AidenAI has spent the last 3 years helping over 30 large enterprises turn the promise of AI into live, measurable business outcomes,” said A91 Partners’ partner Kaushik Anand.

AidenAI’s Bet On Frontier AI Engineering

Alongside its platform expansion, AidenAI plans to build a team of more than 1,000 frontier AI engineers through its AidenAI Builder Academy.

The academy is designed to develop forward-deployed engineering talent that can work directly with enterprise clients to build and deploy production-ready AI applications using the company’s platform and frontier AI models.

The expansion comes as enterprises increasingly explore agentic AI applications to automate complex, multi-step workflows across functions such as finance, insurance, healthcare and human resources.

AidenAI aims to tap this demand by combining AI agents, enterprise software modernisation and specialised engineering services.

This comes as the broader Indian enterprise AI market, which was valued at $11 Bn in 2025, is projected to reach $71 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s Bharat AI Startups Report 2026. 

The Inc42 Take: Can AidenAI Scale Its Enterprise AI Platform?

As more companies adopt GenAI in their daily operations, demand is growing for providers that can build and deploy AI solutions at an enterprise scale.

AidenAI is positioning itself at this intersection via its AI Builder Platform and engineering-led deployment model. Its presence across six countries and a client base of over 30 enterprises provide an early indication of market traction.

However, the startup’s ability to scale will depend on how effectively it can standardise its platform across enterprise customers with different technology infrastructure and business requirements.

item.title: Cosine Robots Bags ₹22.4 Cr To Scale Robotics Hardware Production
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: Bengaluru-based robotics hardware startup Cosine Robots has raised ₹22.4 Cr (about $2.4 Mn) in a funding round led by Avaana…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based robotics hardware startup Cosine Robots has raised ₹22.4 Cr (about $2.4 Mn) in a funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors.

The startup will use the fresh capital to scale its new R&D and production facility in Bengaluru, expand its engineering team, and accelerate development of its integrated servo actuator portfolio.

Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas in 2024, Cosine Robots develops actuators and motion systems for robotic applications.

Actuators convert energy into physical movement, helping control how precisely robotic joints move and how much turning force, or torque, they produce. 

“Our goal is to make high-quality robotics more accessible. This funding will help us strengthen our research and development and establish production capabilities for actuators designed and built by our team,” cofounder and CEO Koshy said.

Building Robotic Motion Hardware

Cosine Robots’ integrated servo actuators combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics, and proprietary control software into a single system. The startup said developing these components together allows it to optimise precision, reliability, torque response, and cost.

Its modular portfolio includes cycloidal and planetary actuators, which use different gearbox designs to address varying torque requirements. These are designed for applications ranging from industrial robotic arms and collaborative robots to quadrupeds and humanoids.

The startup said its proprietary control architecture combines dual-position sensing with a 25 kHz control loop, executing 25,000 updates per second to regulate movement and torque.

Cosine Robots aims to supply global robot manufacturers with an alternative to established actuator suppliers, competing on performance and cost.

The funding comes at a time when investments in robotics and automation startups are picking up. Last week, Botsync raised $11 Mn in an IvyCap Ventures-led round to upgrade its factory automation software and mobile robots, and expand its engineering and project delivery teams in India.

Earlier this year, industrial robotics startup Anscer Robotics raised ₹45 Cr in its Series A round  to advance its product platform, scale US market operations, expand global partner network, and deepen international footprint.

item.title: Ex-Sequoia Investor Sudhanshu Mishra Launches Agentic AI Startup Demi AI
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: Former Sequoia Capital India investor Sudhanshu Mishra has launched an agentic AI startup called Demi.AI in the US, seeking to…
item.content:encoded:
Former Sequoia Capital India investor Sudhanshu Mishra has launched an agentic AI startup called Demi.AI in the US, seeking to build an AI assistant that can anticipate users’ requirements and complete work before being explicitly instructed.

Mishra announced the launch of Demi’s invite-only beta earlier today on social media. He positioned it as an “AI assistant that lives on your Mac, learns how you work, and does the work before you ask”.

Demi’s other cofounder is Mishra’s college roommate Logan Ford and currently employs about 10 people. Demi was set up in June 2025. 

Mishra was earlier associated with Sequoia Capital as an investor. He worked on early-stage investments, primarily leading the firm’s crypto-focused efforts. He subsequently joined Paradigm, a crypto-focused investment firm, as an investment partner.

In his launch announcement, Mishra said the idea behind Demi was to reduce the effort users currently need to put into making AI tools useful, including setting up workflows, providing context and figuring out which tasks to delegate.

Unlike conventional AI assistants that largely respond to individual prompts, Demi aims to continuously build an understanding of users’ work and identify tasks that need attention.

How Does Demi Work?

Demi builds context from users’ meetings, connected applications and even their computer screens to understand ongoing projects, conversations and work patterns.

Based on this context, it tracks commitments, deadlines and recurring tasks, and proactively surfaces reminders or prepares the next steps. For instance, if a user promises to share a document during a meeting, Demi can identify the commitment, locate relevant information and prepare a follow-up email.

The platform can also handle repetitive administrative work, including drafting email responses, preparing meeting briefs, capturing meeting notes, updating customer relationship management (CRM) systems and tracking customer follow-ups.

The agentic platform then executes these tasks either through its cloud-based computer or natively on a user’s Mac through their browser. Moreover, users do not need to create custom workflows or write instructions for individual skills to get started.

The platform still retains a human approval layer and messages, commitments and important changes to records are presented to users for approval before they are executed. According to its website, its individual paid plan starts at $25 per month, while team pricing is customised.

Agentic AI has emerged as the biggest buzz word across the global tech ecosystem with most enterprises and individuals exploring ways to automate their workflows using AI.

According to Grand View Research, the global enterprise agentic AI market is projected to reach $24.5 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 46.2%. 

Investor interest in agentic AI is also accelerating as a new crop of startups look to automate workflows across varied enterprise applications. For instance, Sol Foundry, founded by former CRED executives, raised $4 Mn from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners and others in September this year to build a proactive AI assistant that acts on commitments made over email.

item.title: Google Cloud Confirms India Job Cuts Amid Restructuring
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: Google Cloud has confirmed that it eliminated approximately 30 roles in India last week, while rejecting rumours of large-scale layoffs…
item.content:encoded:
Google Cloud has confirmed that it eliminated approximately 30 roles in India last week, while rejecting rumours of large-scale layoffs at the company.

Responding to a post on X alleging “huge layoffs at Google India”, Google Cloud India described the move as a “small organizational change” involving a reprioritisation of work.

“These rumors are totally inaccurate,” the company said. It did not disclose which teams or functions were affected.

Google Cloud provides cloud computing infrastructure, data analytics, and AI services to businesses, including startups.

The clarification follows an anonymous post on workplace forum Blind alleging sudden cuts across Google’s India-based Cloud teams. The author, who claimed to be a Bengaluru-based Google employee, alleged that some workers had received 24-hour deadlines to resign or face termination, with one month’s severance.

The post also alleged that some employees were being placed on preliminary performance improvement plans that restricted internal transfers, while their US counterparts had not been affected.

Inc42 could not independently verify these claims. The Blind post also referred to internal speculation about voluntary exits or further layoffs in Google’s Platforms and Devices division in January 2027. 

Inc42 has reached out to Google India for details on the affected roles, exit terms, and the allegations. The story will be updated when the company responds.


Google’s Global Workforce Restructuring

The development comes amid Google’s broader workforce restructuring as the technology giant continues to increase investments in AI.

It earlier offered voluntary exit packages to employees in several international markets, including Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland, following similar programmes in the US and the UK, Reuters reported earlier this month.

The voluntary buyout programmes reportedly covered multiple teams, while Google Cloud and DeepMind appeared to be excluded from those rounds. These voluntary programmes are distinct from the role eliminations Google Cloud has now confirmed in India.

Google has previously undertaken larger workforce reductions in the country. In February 2023, the company laid off 453 employees across departments in India, following Alphabet’s announcement of 12,000 job cuts globally.

The latest cuts come alongside Google’s expansion of its cloud and AI infrastructure in India.

In October last year, the company announced plans to invest $15 Bn in an AI hub in Visakhapatnam over 2026-2030. The project includes gigawatt-scale data centre infrastructure, energy supply, and expanded fibre-optic connectivity to support Google’s services and customers building AI applications.

Google broke ground on the hub in April this year, working with AdaniConneX and Nxtra by Airtel. The company said the infrastructure would provide computing capacity for startups and large enterprises to scale AI services.

item.title: Sarvam AI Launches Dictation API For English, 22 Indian Languages
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: AI unicorn Sarvam AI has launched Sarvam Dictate, an API that lets developers add voice dictation in English and 22…
item.content:encoded:
AI unicorn Sarvam AI has launched Sarvam Dictate, an API that lets developers add voice dictation in English and 22 Indian languages to their applications.

Priced at ₹0.50 per minute of audio, the service combines speech recognition with transcript editing in a single API call. It is designed to turn spoken inputs into text for messages, documents, and business records.

Dictate pairs the startup’s Saaras V4 speech recognition model with a version of its Sarvam 105B large language model trained for dictation. The first transcribes the audio, while the second edits the resulting text.

Announcing the launch on X, Sarvam claimed that Dictate outperformed Google’s Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and AssemblyAI Dictation on a set of real-world dictation tests.

According to the startup, for English dictations of up to one minute, the API required 40% fewer character edits than Gemini 3.5 Transcribe. Across Indian languages and Hinglish, the reduction stood at 47%.

For longer English dictations, Dictate required 11% fewer character edits than Gemini and 17% fewer than AssemblyAI.

Sarvam highlighted that its Dictate API is designed to account for the way people naturally speak, and can handle speakers switching between English and Indian languages mid-sentence, correcting themselves, and making false starts. It also cleans up pauses and repetitions to produce a more refined transcript.

Developers can provide up to 1,000 names and technical terms per request, alongside contextual information such as customer relationship management (CRM) records, product lists, and a description of the situation.

They can also specify formatting preferences and choose how Indian languages and English appear in the output, including native scripts or Latin letters.

The API supports live dictation and uploaded recordings of up to an hour, returning both the raw transcript and edited text. Its documented applications include chat messages, sales records, forms, and meeting minutes.

As per Sarvam, Dictate has already been tested through Kivi, its dictation application, where users have dictated more than 30 Mn words since launch.

Voice AI Gains Ground

The launch comes as AI developers increasingly integrate voice interfaces into applications for documentation, customer interactions, and data entry. Potential uses span customer support, telehealth, medical documentation, and sales record updates, extending the scope for Sarvam’s multilingual voice AI offerings.

India’s linguistic diversity presents a significant opportunity for voice AI, with the domestic market projected to reach $1.8 Bn by 2030, according to Nasscom. Startups are developing speech-to-text models to tap this demand for multilingual applications.

Earlier today, voice AI infrastructure startup Murf AI launched Finch, a streaming speech-to-text model that it claims ranks first across 11 Indian languages on the Voice of India benchmark, ahead of models from ElevenLabs, OpenAI, xAI, and Microsoft. Murf claims Finch delivers a time-to-final-segment of 50 milliseconds and supports code-mixed speech and optional voice isolation.

Sarvam’s latest launch also follows the rollout of Token Factory, a platform that gives enterprises API access to its own models alongside global open-weight models, including Google’s Gemma and China’s DeepSeek.

Token Factory drew questions over whether Sarvam had used government-subsidised GPU capacity allocated for developing homegrown models to host foreign models. The startup subsequently clarified that the platform runs on privately procured GPUs.

Reiterating its focus on model development, Sarvam said it will launch more models across vision, speech, and edge AI over the next two weeks.

item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: CortexSpark Ventures, founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, has launched its debut fund, Viksit Bharat Fund-I,…
item.content:encoded:
CortexSpark Ventures, founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, has launched its debut fund, Viksit Bharat Fund-I, targeting a ₹1,000 Cr (about $107 Mn) corpus to back deeptech and AI startups.

The fund has an additional ₹400 Cr greenshoe option, taking its potential size to ₹1,400 Cr (about $150 Mn). It has secured SEBI registration as a Category II AIF under the name CortexSpark Ventures Alpha Fund, the firm said.

The fund plans to back around 20 startups, with an average cheque size of $4 Mn to $5 Mn.

The fund will back startups working on proprietary technologies across six sectors – spacetech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech and bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials.

“India has built world-class technology services companies. The next opportunity is to create globally competitive technology product companies driven by original research and intellectual property,” Peshwa said.

Peshwa is an IIT Kanpur alumnus with nearly three decades of experience in software, banking technology and startup investing. He was involved in developing Infosys Finacle and has made more than 30 angel investments, mainly in AI and deeptech startups.

Khanduri holds degrees from IIT (BHU) and IIM Lucknow, as well as an MBA from Wharton. He previously worked with Citigroup, Infosys, and Standard Chartered Bank in global capital markets and alternative investments.

CortexSpark Ventures’ Investment Thesis

CortexSpark Ventures will focus on startups with proprietary technology, strong technical foundations, experienced founders, and clear commercialisation plans. It plans to assess potential investments through scientific evaluation and commercial due diligence, particularly in sectors that involve longer development cycles and higher capital requirements.

The firm is also developing CortexSpark OS, an AI-based platform to support deal sourcing, screening, due diligence, and portfolio monitoring.

Beyond funding, it will help portfolio startups with product development, hiring and business growth, while connecting them with enterprise customers, international markets and follow-on investors.

The fund’s investment committee will be chaired by Manoj Kohli, former country head of SoftBank Group and former CEO and MD of Bharti Airtel.

Its advisory committee will include two Padma Shri-awardee scientists – N Vedachalam, former director of ISRO’s Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, and Ashutosh Sharma, former secretary of the Department of Science and Technology and Institute Chair Professor at IIT Kanpur.

The fund launch comes amid rising investor interest in India’s deeptech ecosystem. Last week, Oister Global launched a ₹600 Cr growth-stage deeptech fund. Meanwhile, Unacademy cofounders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are also reportedly raising a ₹700 Cr fund, Longshot Capital, to invest in AI and deeptech startups.

According to Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals during the quarter, up 176% from $105 Mn across 29 deals a year earlier. This compared with a 5% increase in overall startup funding to $2.2 Bn.

item.title: D2C Brands Build A Multiverse
item.dc:creator: Meha Agarwal
item.description: Last week, the parent of Bombay Shaving Company, Visage Lines Personal Care, made an unexpected move by entering the recovery…
item.content:encoded:
Last week, the parent of Bombay Shaving Company, Visage Lines Personal Care, made an unexpected move by entering the recovery and wellness market with the launch of rE, a new brand offering massage guns, foam rollers, scalp massagers and other recovery products.

The move is particularly interesting because the two categories are not just poles apart but also huge markets with enormous scope for vertical expansion. 

Let’s quickly steal a glance at some numbers. 

While the total personal care market in India is set to touch $40 Bn+ by 2034, another lucrative category is gaining ground. Once restricted to sports medicine and professional athletes, at-home recovery products (including percussion massagers, foam rollers, thermal therapy) have become everyday wellness essentials for people grappling with stress, poor sleep and posture, and muscle fatigue. In fact, some reports already peg the market for at-home recovery and massage devices alone at over $400 Mn. 

But Bombay Shaving Company isn’t the only one that decided to slide into untested waters. Earlier this year, we witnessed men’s fashion brand Snitch foray into the travel gear market with their ‘luggage’ category. 

Cult.fit, a widely recognised gym chain, is positioning its sneakers for “non-gym, all-day moves”. In fact, Cult has already created a large portfolio of daily athleisure, relaxation and recovery gadgets, hydration products and more. 

These aren’t new brands trying to find their product-market fit but the ones that have already made it to crossing ₹1,000 Cr in revenue or are running their annualised run rates quite close to that number. 

This makes us ponder: are D2C brands simply getting more ambitious, or is staying in their own lane becoming a little too limiting for their growth ambitions? How are these brands deciding which new categories to enter and what amount of resources to allocate? Let’s check out…

Opening A New Turf: A Need Or Ambition?

It’s both. 

According to Inc42’s D2C 3.0 Report 2026, India’s D2C gross merchandise value (GMV) is projected to reach $310 Bn+ by 2031, growing at a CAGR of roughly 37% from $65 Bn in 2026. 

Yet, several prominent Indian D2C and consumer brands remain in the red — often despite strong top-line growth — as expenses, customer acquisition, or expansion costs continue to weigh on their bottom lines. 

The reason is simple: Once a brand reaches the limits of growth in its core market, it needs new avenues to expand. Launching a new brand allows it to tap into fresh categories, attract new customers and generate more revenue from its existing customer base. Ideally, the smart moves are adjacent rather than unrelated, so the playbook and learnings carry over. Besides, rising customer acquisition costs make it imperative for a brand to sell across categories. 

“It’s similar to how wealth management firms operate. Once a customer is acquired, the same firm can offer everything from FDs and broking services to F&O trading and pension plans. So, why spend more on acquiring new customers when you can sell more to the ones you already have?” said a sectoral expert.

This, however, doesn’t mean that a consumer who trusts a brand for one product will automatically buy everything else it launches. This is also where the choice of category becomes important. Brands need to identify their own strengths that can work to their advantage even in an entirely new market.

Varun Gupta, the cofounder of rE and CMO of Bombay Shaving Company, cited three key factors behind entering a new market.

“One is we are very consumer-obsessed. We talk to the consumers a lot. We understand how they use products, what their journeys are in life. Second, we know how to tell great stories. And third is our sourcing and product are extremely robust and efficient,” Gupta said.

But flip the coin, and a rather exciting side of this story emerges.

Until a few years ago, entering a new category meant building distribution networks, spending heavily on marketing and waiting months, sometimes years, to see whether consumers would even bite. Today, quick commerce can put a new product in front of consumers across multiple cities within weeks.

Celebrity partnerships are also rewriting the marketing playbook. Instead of spending a fortune on endorsements, brands are onboarding celebrities as equity-holding cofounders. With this, they are turning their influence into a long-term customer acquisition engine.

The Brand Architecture Dilemma

Two brands in different categories don’t necessarily mean two separate companies running two entirely different operations.

“When a new brand is launched, functions such as HR, finance, supply chain, warehouses and even ecommerce relationships can remain common. So, it starts with having a different category marketing team. Everything else is shared,” said Gupta.

And this is precisely what makes the multi-brand model tempting for companies that have an established core operations team. 

According to the founder of TDV Partners, Ujwal Sutaria, customer data, performance marketing expertise, distribution relationships and backend operations can carry over. However, product expertise and credibility in the new category still have to be earned. 

Therefore, brands must spend time identifying what deserves a separate name and what can continue running behind the scenes as one business. 

This is crucial because while sharing resources can make expansion more economical, maintaining multiple identities means multiple sets of expectations. And that’s where the excitement of building a brand portfolio begins to meet the realities of running one.

Beware Of The Burn 

For brands already struggling to turn growing revenues into profits, one wrong bet could make the burn even worse.

As highlighted by 3One4 Capital’s founding partner Pranav Pai, each category operates on its own set of variables: repeat cycle, ticket size, gross margin band, trust threshold, regulatory burdens, and service obligation. 

One vertical may run at low ticket sizes, high repeat and moderate margin, with replenishment measured in weeks. Another may be a single high-ticket purchase carrying warranty, after-sales commitments and a replacement cycle measured in years. 

So, even with an identical customer, the economics for both are not always comparable, and working capital, team composition and channel mix shift accordingly.

Brand architecture is another constraint. A brand is a living entity with its own appeal and its own approachability, and it has to hold trust for millions of customers rather than reflect a single founder’s preferences. 

“Expanding into a segment where it has little credibility could dilute the trust and reputation built in its core market, a cost that is difficult to quantify at the time of launch,” Pai said.

While launching and testing new brands has become cheaper in India, getting customers to return and buy again remains just as challenging. This is where one needs to observe whether a brand can stand on its own financially, operate under dedicated leadership, offer something genuinely different and benefit from the parent company’s existing infrastructure.

The success of multi-brand companies also depends on how efficiently their supply chains, distribution and operations are being managed. The winners, therefore, won’t necessarily be those launching the most brands, but those who hit the bull’s eye on what consumers want.

THE STARTUP SPOTLIGHT | HOW AMNECT IS REINVENTING NUTRITION WITH GUMMIES

  • Amnect Care is addressing age-related health concerns through its portfolio of specialised, sugar-free gummies targeting bone health, joint mobility, digestion, sleep quality and overall wellbeing, positioning them as convenient alternatives to traditional supplements. 
  • The startup offers four key product lines: Bone Care, Joint Care, Mind & Sleep Care, and Motion Care, priced from ₹699 to ₹999 for 30-gummy packs. Its formulations combine vitamins, minerals, botanical extracts and clinically studied ingredients.
  • Amnect currently operates with 4 SKUs and clocks an average monthly recurring revenue (MRR) of ₹1 Lakh, with sales evenly split between its own website and offline retail, with each channel contributing 50%.

THE DEEP DIVE

Ecommerce Buzz

Aman Gupta’s New Beauty Brand: The boAt cofounder has launched men’s personal care brand H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man), along with actor Ranveer Singh. The brand offers eight products across face, body and hair care with formulations designed for Indian skin and climatic conditions.

Henfruit Closes Maiden Capital Raise: The egg startup bagged $15 Mn in its first external round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures. It plans to expand distribution beyond its current 15-city footprint and increase production capacity.

Style Union Bags ₹485 Cr: The omnichannel fashion brand’s Series E round was co-led by Venturi Partners and Elev8 Venture Partners. It will use the capital to expand its offline store network across key metros in West and North India. 

Urban Company Closes ₹2,500 Cr QIP: The home services platform attracted bids worth over ₹15,000 Cr for the QIP. It plans to allocate ₹600 Cr towards expanding InstaHelp’s service professional ecosystem, while building its Native products business.

Flipkart Weighs On Walmart Growth: The timing of Flipkart’s Big Billion Days sale reduced Walmart International’s Q3 FY27 sales growth by around 500 bps, with the impact expected to reverse in Q4. Its net sales rose 7% YoY to $35.9 Bn, while ecommerce sales declined 2%.

Bewakoof Cofounder Launches Save8: After stepping down as CEO, Prabhkiran Singh has launched an AI-powered shopping assistant that compares prices, coupons, cashback and payment offers across ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, covering over 1,000 online stores.

item.title: Manufacturing Startups To Watch: 5 Startups That Caught Our Eye In November
item.dc:creator: Ankush Das
item.description: India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond merely assembling finished products. Homegrown startups are developing specialised components, propulsion systems and machinery…
item.content:encoded:
India’s manufacturing story is moving beyond merely assembling finished products. Homegrown startups are developing specialised components, propulsion systems and machinery to power sectors from oil to telecom and from aerospace to railways.

Policy support is also deepening. In November, the Union Cabinet approved a ₹2,814 Cr scheme to set up domestic lithium and nickel processing plants, part of a drive to cut imports and keep value addition within the country. Simultaneously, the government moved to prohibit the export of lithium-ion battery ‘black mass’ so recycled critical metals stay in India. 

Private capital is moving in the same direction. Indian deeptech startups raised nearly $665 Mn across 94 deals in the first nine months of 2026. And the past few weeks have only added to this momentum. From Bharat Semi’s $24 Mn fundraise to build smart sensors for robots to Nova Spectral AI bagging ₹21.2 Cr for indigenous infrared sensor chips, investors are flocking to the sector. 

Combined, these developments are creating new opportunities for startups looking to power India’s industrial growth. 

Against this backdrop, Inc42 is back with the latest edition of its ‘Five Manufacturing Startups To Watch’. This edition features new-age tech ventures working across rare-earth-free electric propulsion, aerospace engines and specialised machinery.

So, without further ado, here are the five manufacturing startups that caught our eye in November

Editor’s Note: This list is not a ranking. It is a curated selection of manufacturing startups that have stood out to the Inc42 editorial team this month.

Viridian Ingni Propulsion | Building Rare-Earth-Free Motors For EVs

Most electric propulsion systems depend on rare-earth magnets, a component largely controlled by China. Export curbs and price shocks in recent years have made that dependence a strategic risk for manufacturers of vehicles, drones and industrial machines.

Enter Viridian Ingni Propulsion, a Chennai-based deeptech startup that is trying to solve India’s overdependence on imported rare-earth metals. Founded in 2024 by Sriram Gopal, the IIT Madras Research Park-incubated startup builds rare-earth-free motors for multiple use cases. 

For e-rickshaws, two-wheelers, HVAC systems and solar pumps, it makes rare-earth-free ferrite motors. Meanwhile, drones, automated guided vehicles and collaborative robots can use its high-power permanent magnet motors. 

Its flagship L3 e-rickshaw motor is a 48V unit with a 1.2 kW power capacity. Its 8 kg motor has a 4.5 Nm rated torque, 2,250 rpm rated speed, and 94% peak efficiency. 

In October 2026, it raised ₹1.47 Cr to move from prototype to pilot production. The Chennai-based startup is looking to disrupt India’s rare earth magnet market, expected to become a $1 Bn opportunity by 2034.

Parsec Aerospace | Developing Next-Generation Aerospace Engines

Aerospace propulsion is dominated by established builders abroad, and early stage engine designers remain rare in India. This is because building indigenous engines requires deep engineering across materials, combustion, and control, and most designs take years to validate.

Parsec Aerospace is a Bengaluru-based startup developing next-generation engines for aerospace applications. Founded in 2025 by Effy John, a former system design engineer at spacetech startup Pixxel, the startup manufactures components for reaction engine systems.

The startup’s small team spans India and France as it works to develop propulsion it believes will underpin future aircraft and spacecraft.

Parsec is in talks to raise around $10 Mn from Nexus Venture Partners. The startup operates in the Indian aerospace propulsion market, expected to become a $530 Mn opportunity by 2031, supported by a growing number of spacetech platforms and ISRO’s strategic initiatives.

Its trajectory will depend on moving from stealth to validated engine hardware and securing customers amid rising investor appetite for early-stage aerospace ventures.

Autocracy Machinery | Manufacturing Trenchers For Indian Needs 

Laying underground networks for optical fibre, water, gas and electricity needs trenching machines, equipment that has historically been imported and often ill-suited for local soil and route conditions.

Autocracy Machinery is a Hyderabad-based manufacturer building trenchers, tractor attachments, aquatic weed harvesters and utility equipment for telecom, solar, water management, agriculture and defence projects. 

Founded in 2020 by IIT Madras alumna Santhoshi Sushma Buddhiraju, the startup grew out of the observation that India imported around $43 Bn worth of machinery a year and relied on foreign machines, which often cost up to $150K each and were not tailored to local conditions.

Today, it offers more than 40 models across 13 product lines, including its indigenously developed RUDRA, GAJA, DHRUVA and VAH trencher range engineered for Indian terrain. Its machines can cut trenches for cables, pipelines and drainage in urban, rural and remote conditions. The startup also exports its products to Africa and the Middle East.

Autocracy operates in the Indian construction equipment market, which could become a $29.50 Bn opportunity by 2034. The startup’s right to win will depend on scaling production for domestic and export projects while helping lower India’s reliance on imported machinery.

Pluto Mobility | Purpose-Built Electric Delivery Vehicles

Most delivery fleets run on conventional two-wheelers designed for personal use. But many of these vehicles struggle under the heavy loads, long shifts and rough handling of ecommerce and quick commerce deliveries.

Gurugram-based EV startup Pluto Mobility is building scooter-sized electric three-wheelers purpose-built for last-mile deliveries. Founded in 2024 by Akshat Bhatia and Himanshu Panda, the startup has designed its vehicle around a tilting tadpole layout with two front wheels for stability under heavy loads.

Pluto Mobility’s prototype vehicle can carry up to 100 kg of cargo, roughly twice the volume of a conventional two-wheeler. It also comes with a 3 kWh swappable battery, offering more than 100 km of daily range, plus a covered canopy for riders. 

The founders built their prototype in November 2024. The startup has since built six minimum viable product units and tested its prototype across more than 2,000 km. It is currently piloting the vehicle with delivery companies, aggregators and third-party logistics firms.

In February 2026, Pluto raised $2 Mn in India’s electric last-mile delivery vehicle market, which is projected to become a $22 Bn opportunity by 2033. 

Tryaksh Innovations | AI-Powered Railway Track Inspection

Railway safety often depends on flagging track defects before they cause accidents. Manual inspections are slow and labour-intensive, and imported monitoring equipment can be costly to deploy across a vast network.

Enter Tryaksh Innovations, a Nagpur-based startup that is building an AI-enabled digital rolling track gauge for railways. Founded in 2025 by Richansh Gour, the startup claims that its device can capture more than 50 track geometry parameters at a resolution of 0.01 mm.

The device comes with AI-powered anomaly detection, which gives track engineers a faster and data-driven alternative to conduct manual inspections and maintenance. It also helps railway crews prioritise repairs before defects escalate into safety risks.

Tryaksh is bootstrapped and supported by an equity-free grant from MeitY Startup Hub’s GENESIS EiR programme, and is incubated at InFED IIM Nagpur. It operates in the broader Indian railway infrastructure maintenance market, which is expected to become a $7.01 Bn opportunity by 2033.

item.content:encoded:
Sarvam Defends Token Factory

Sarvam is standing its ground. Under fire for hosting Chinese AI models on its inference service, the AI unicorn has clarified that it is creating a new commercial opportunity. The startup has also reiterated plans to double down on indigenous LLMs. 

Sarvam Hits Back: Pushing back against criticism that Token Factory relies on taxpayer’s money to host models like DeepSeek and Kimi, Sarvam said that the offering relies strictly on privately procured GPUs. The startup said it received no direct cash payouts under IndiaAI Mission, and subsidies ended in March and only came in the form of subsidised hardware. 

The Case For Inference: Cofounder Pratyush Kumar said that most of India’s current token demand is served by overseas players. As per him, building domestic inference capacity could reduce this dependence and help local enterprises address issues like higher latency and data residency. He also said that inference is creating a new commercial business for Sarvam, which will generate vital revenue for funding its capex-intensive AI development.

The Sovereign Pitch: To prove that inference hosting has not diluted its core research mission, Sarvam also rolled out Sarvam-105B-1711 – its upgraded open-weight model with sharper reasoning, tool-use, and Indian-language capabilities. The unicorn said that it will roll out new vision, speech, and edge models over the coming two weeks. 

The Lingering Questions: That said, Sarvam will have to carry the cost of idle capacity initially as Token Factory scales its inference business. Then, there is data risk, as the AI unicorn currently offers zero data retention only on request. On top of this, new and deep-pocketed players are also disrupting the inference space with regular and niche offerings. 

With much on its plate, can Sarvam balance commercial hosting with indigenous R&D? Let’s find out…

From The Editor’s Desk

Jensen Huang Back At NVIDIA

  • NVIDIA’s board has reinstated cofounder Jensen Huang as the chipmaker’s president and CEO. Post his return, interim CEO Colette Kress will transition back to the role of CFO, while Harvey Jones will remain the chair of the board.
  • The stunning reversal comes less than a fortnight after Huang resigned as the CEO of NVIDIA, following he had three extramarital affairs – one of which involved a woman accused of spying for China.
  • Shares of the chipmaker surged more than 30% after the announcement. Meanwhile, NVIDIA has also constituted a panel to oversee compliance and national security risks. It has also begun searching for a chief compliance officer.

Matters.AI Bags ₹115 Cr

  • The AI-native data security platform, formerly OptiQ.AI, has raised around $12 Mn in its pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners to bolster R&D, expand its North American sales operations and ramp up leadership hiring.
  •  Founded in 2023, Matters.AI is building an autonomous “AI security engineer for data”. Its platform helps enterprises identify sensitive information and tracks how agents interact with this data. It claims to serve 50 clients and has raised ₹175 Cr to date.
  • The fundraise comes as cyber attackers use LLMs to find vulnerabilities in enterprise systems, spurring the demand for tools that can remediate AI misuse. This is pushing the broader Indian AI market to become a $126 Bn opportunity by 2030.

VinFast Vs Cab Drivers

  • Police authorities in Bengaluru’s Electronic City have registered an FIR against the president of Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta, G Narayana Swamy, and others for destroying the recruitment posters of the EV giant’s ride-hailing arm Green SM.
  • Swamy and a group of unidentified cab drivers allegedly barged into a private hotel in Hosa Road and vandalised the property by tearing up banners and abusing company representatives. This was allegedly done to impede Green SM’s recruitment drive.
  • This comes a week after the state government directed transport department officials to stop registering new Green SM taxis until further orders. However, around 100 vehicles operated by the company have already been registered to ply on the roads in the state. 

RBI’s New Fintech Safeguards

  • The Reserve Bank of India has proposed a new ‘Stop Switch’ to curb online payment frauds. The new switch will allow users to to disable all outgoing debits, new payment mandates and new UPI app registrations.
  • In addition, the central bank has also pitched a voluntary Trusted Person Mechanism for high-value transfers. Under this facility, account holders can nominate an adult as an additional authentication layer for transactions above a specified threshold.
  • The new safeguards are part of RBI’s draft new rules for financial institutions. Under this, banks will also have to offer customers granular controls over their digital payment channels. The proposed framework is expected to come into effect by July 2027.

Meta’s Regulatory Crisis

  • The I4C has advised users to avoid exchanging official, financial and other sensitive information via WhatsApp Web. The watchdog has warned that active WhatsApp Web browser sessions could be misused to access user accounts and access their contacts.
  • Separately, members of the Indian Youth Congress protested against Meta India’s content moderation policies. Protestors accused the social media giant of political bias, non-transparent content takedowns and restricting accounts linked to opposition figures
  • This comes as Meta is facing a regulatory storm in the country. Earlier this year, a report found that paid adverts, promoting CSAM, were running on Instagram India. Following this, the Centre pulled up the platform and directed it to comply with local laws.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

Can CosmoChute Build A Shared Taxi Service To Moon?

Every lunar mission today needs bespoke systems to transport, power and protect its payload. This can make surface operations on the moon slow and expensive. To solve this, CosmoChute is building a reusable platform that multiple customers can share.

A Modular Platform: Founded in 2026, CosmoChute is developing LEAP (Lunar Exploration and Access Platform), a modular system for transporting and deploying payloads on the moon. Its stack combines EPOC, a modular rover; OASYS, a towable trailer; and Cartridge, a payload-survival system. 

Made For Lunar Missions: EPOC comes with autonomous navigation and a robotic arm for payload handling and potential surface operations. OASYS adds cargo capacity via payload bays, while Cartridge aims to protect payloads from extreme lunar temperatures. The rover is designed to stay on the Moon, which can also transport payloads delivered by later missions. 

This one-size-fits-all approach could make lunar experiments, commercial hardware and scientific instruments cheaper to deploy. 

Still In Infancy: Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the startup is currently building ground infrastructure to develop and validate its lunar mobility platform. It plans to test development models in early-2027 and work towards flight qualification by 2028. With the lunar rover and mobility vehicle market projected to become a $4.1 Bn opportunity by 2032, can CosmoChute’s reusable system survive the moon’s harsh environment?

item.content:encoded:
Early backer and hedge fund Steadview Capital has sold 1.27 Cr shares of omnichannel eyewear giant Lenskart via multiple block deals for ₹920.6 Cr.

As per NSE data, Steadview Capital, via two funds – Steadview Capital Mauritius Ltd and LTR Focus Fund, sold the shares at ₹725 apiece to rake in the amount. 

The shares that flooded the market were lapped up by Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale. While Goldman Sachs, via two affiliates, picked up 65.2 Lakh shares for a sum of ₹472.8 Cr, Societe Generale bought the remaining 61.8 Lakh shares for ₹447.8 Cr.

Steadview Capital Mauritius Ltd held a 3.31% stake, or 5.8 Cr shares, in the eyewear giant at the end of September 2026. With the latest block deals, the hedge fund has offloaded nearly a fifth (22% to be precise) of its shareholding in Lenskart. 

The latest move adds to a series of stake sales by Lenskart’s early investors in recent months. Just last month, Alpha Wave Ventures sold Lenskart shares worth ₹1,704.8 Cr. Prior to this in August, the VC firm also offloaded 2.94 Cr shares of the omnichannel eyewear giant in multiple block deals for ₹1,856.8 Cr.

Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) also sold Lenskart shares worth ₹2,390.6 Cr in September, while SoftBank offloaded 4.5 Cr shares of the eyewear giant, worth ₹2,887.9 Cr, in August.

An extended bull run for the stock has provided a fertile ground for investors to cash in. The company’s stock touched an all-time high of ₹767.40 on November 5, and has zoomed over 58.5% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. 

This surge has come on the back of robust financial performance. Lenskart saw its consolidated net profit zoom 124.7% to ₹232.5 Cr in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27) compared to ₹103.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, operating revenue also rose 35.7% to ₹2,845 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹2,096.1 Cr in Q2 FY26.

item.title: RBI Proposes ‘Stop Switch’ To Block Digital Payment Frauds
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed a set of safeguards against electronic payment frauds, including an account-wide ‘Stop…
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed a set of safeguards against electronic payment frauds, including an account-wide ‘Stop Switch’ and a ‘Trusted Person Mechanism’ (TPM) for high-value transactions.

The central bank has invited feedback on the draft directions by December 14, 2026, with the proposed rules set to come into effect from July 1, 2027.

Under the Draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026, banks will have to provide a ‘Stop Switch’ that allows customers to immediately disable all outgoing debits, new payment mandates and new UPI app registrations.

The switch will not block incoming credits or existing standing instructions. Customers will be able to activate, modify or deactivate it through bank branches, ATMs, mobile apps, internet banking and interactive voice response (IVR) services.

Banks will also have to ensure that re-enabling digital payment channels or deactivating the Stop Switch requires at least the same level of authentication as its activation.

The RBI has also proposed a voluntary Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM) for high-value transfers. Under this facility, account holders can nominate an adult as an additional authentication layer for transactions above a specified threshold.

The nominated person will have to approve such transactions within a one-hour window. However, the trusted person will not have any legal authority over the account or access to its details.

Banks will be responsible for verifying the identity and eligibility of nominated individuals. Any activation or modification of the TPM will also be subject to a 24-hour cooling-off period.

The RBI had first floated a similar proposal in June this year, suggesting an additional authentication layer for digital transactions above ₹10,000 made by citizens aged 70 and above.

Beyond these measures, banks will have to offer customers granular controls over their digital payment channels. These will include options to enable or disable individual channels, set time windows for their deactivation and establish transaction limits per transfer, per beneficiary or through aggregate daily caps.

The draft also proposes that all digital payment channels remain disabled by default during customer onboarding and be activated only with explicit consent.

Further, newly issued physical and virtual cards will be restricted by default to domestic contact-based ATM and point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Newly enabled digital payment channels will also be subject to a transfer limit determined by the bank for the first 24 hours.

Earlier this year, the central bank issued directions requiring banks to compensate eligible victims of digital payment frauds. The latest proposals take a more preventive approach, giving customers greater control over payment channels and adding authentication safeguards to help stop fraudulent transactions before they are completed.

item.title: NVIDIA Reinstates Jensen Huang As President & CEO
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: NVIDIA has reinstated cofounder Jensen Huang as its president and chief executive officer (CEO). The reappointment comes 11 days after…
item.content:encoded:
NVIDIA has reinstated cofounder Jensen Huang as its president and chief executive officer (CEO). The reappointment comes 11 days after he resigned from the company amid reports of a foreign intelligence effort targeting him.

In a statement today, the company informed that its board of directors unanimously approved the reinstatement, effective immediately, following a series of discussions and meetings with him. The board said it was satisfied with Huang’s candour and ability to lead the company moving forward.

Pertinent to mention that the company also took into account inputs from senior US government officials, based on which it felt confident that the reinstatement won’t pose any threat to the country’s security risk.

The development reverses the leadership transition announced on November 12, when Huang resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board with immediate effect. Huang’s exit came after the revelations of extramarital affairs, one of which involved a woman accused of spying for China.

In a letter written to NVIDIA employees, Huang apologised for the issue. Before the allegations of the third affair came to light, the company’s board met on November 12, and voted to oust Jensen Huang. 

At the time, Nvidia appointed its executive vice president and chief financial officer (CFO) Colette Kress as interim CEO.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said in a post on November 17.

Post his return, Kress will transition back to the role of CFO, while Harvey Jones will remain chair of the board.

Nvidia said its board had formed a committee comprising only independent directors to investigate the matter. The committee has retained independent legal counsel, and the investigation will continue to its conclusion. Huang has agreed to cooperate with the probe.

The company has also constituted a separate National Security and Export Control Committee, comprising independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

Additionally, NVIDIA is beginning a search for a chief compliance officer (CCO), who will oversee compliance across the company and report to its Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. The company said it would continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

item.title: Home Ministry Warns Of WhatsApp Web Misuse, Advises Against Sensitive Work
item.dc:creator: Md Zakariya Khan
item.description: The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Ministry of Home Affairs, has advised users to avoid exchanging official,…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Ministry of Home Affairs, has advised users to avoid exchanging official, financial, confidential, or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web, warning that active browser sessions could be misused to access their accounts. 

In a recent advisory, I4C’s National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said such access could allow attackers to read messages, impersonate account holders, and access contacts and group conversations. They could then exploit the account holder’s trusted identity for fraud, phishing, and social engineering.

The agency urged users to exercise particular caution on office computers, shared systems, public computers, and devices accessible to other people. It also stressed that closing a browser tab or window should not be treated as logging out of WhatsApp Web. 

Notably, WhatsApp Web allows users to access the messaging service through a computer browser after linking their account.

Precautions For Web Users

I4C has recommended the following measures:

  • Avoid sensitive work: Government, organisational, financial, confidential, or other sensitive information should preferably not be exchanged through WhatsApp Web on computers.
  • Limit active sessions: Avoid leaving WhatsApp Web logged in when it is not required, particularly on office or shared computers.
  • Log out manually: Log out after completing your work rather than simply closing the browser tab or window.
  • Use private browsing cautiously: If temporary access is unavoidable, use incognito or private browsing mode on a trusted computer and manually log out before closing the browser.
  • Avoid untrusted computers: Do not access WhatsApp Web from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers, or other untrusted systems.
  • Watch for unusual activity: Treat unexpected messages sent from your account, unusual replies from contacts, or unexplained activity seriously.
  • Keep devices secure: Update operating systems, browsers, and security software, and avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files, pirated software, and untrusted applications.

The warning follows an earlier I4C alert about a fraud campaign targeting company directors, finance professionals, and businesspersons through WhatsApp account takeovers.

In August, the agency described how attackers circulated malicious ZIP files disguised as account statements or communications from the RBI and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Opening the files on a Windows computer installed malware that could hijack an active WhatsApp Web session.

I4C advised companies to independently verify urgent fund-transfer instructions or requests to change bank account details through a direct voice call or in-person confirmation before acting.

Separately, I4C has also flagged the use of AI agents in attacks targeting financial institutions.

The agency recently warned banks, NBFCs, and fintech startups about attackers exploiting unpatched software and misconfigured internet-facing servers to access financial infrastructure.

The warnings also come amid efforts to strengthen safeguards on messaging platforms. It was reported last month that platforms including WhatsApp and Telegram were preparing to implement the Department of Telecommunications’ SIM-binding mandate.
